svg.text: CHISUM · Wheelhouse forward bay and gallery: arrangement and structure
Johansson Shipyard · JS2-211 · revision 0 · 12 November 2026 · newbuilding No. 1 · general arrangement revision D
NOTHING IS BUILT OVER A WINDOW
Every knee stands in line with a bulkhead of the deck below, clear of every opening.

THE KNEES AGAINST THE WINDOWS
x -2.995 m: on the bulkhead master's suite / stair; 1.01 m long, 0.79 m deep; the
nearest window 0.60 m away
x -2.085 m: on the bulkhead stair / ship's office; 1.56 m long, 0.79 m deep; the nearest
window 0.78 m away
x +0.400 m: on the bulkhead ship's office / pilot cabin; 1.56 m long, 0.79 m deep; the
nearest window 0.80 m away
x +2.995 m: on the bulkhead pilot cabin / chief engineer; 1.01 m long, 0.79 m deep; the
nearest window 0.60 m away
The rule (steel.bay_knees): a knee stands only in line with a bulkhead of the deck below;
the build stops if one is nearer a window's opening than 0.30 m; every knee's foot ends
above the windows' heads (0.32 m here), though none is over one. Between knees more than 1.6
m apart a beam under the plate (x -0.84, +1.70): it comes no lower than the face bar, 0.98 m
over the windows' heads.
WHAT THE BAY IS FOR
The console block stood against the forward bulkhead. A chief constructor, of that: it
must be reached from its other side for electrical work and maintenance. The middle of
the bridge front is built 1.00 m forward as a bay with a canted corner each side (the
owner's photograph of the Finnarrow: "that protruding part forward on the bridge"); the
block keeps its place and stands free, with a way 1.00 m wide before it.
The way is entered from either side: to starboard past the watchkeeper's table, 0.70 m;
to port 1.07 m (0.87 m between the binocular box on the block's end and the handrail).
The settee, which closed the port way to 0.46 m, stands in the port wing against its
after wall, 0.15 m from the door and 2.03 m clear of the fire hose box. In the block's
back a service door for each of its five bays opens into the way.
The block is fed from below now: its cables came down two window mullions into its back;
they go down the same mullions to the deck, through it in a transit, under it, and up
through a transit in the block's bottom. Two 24 V ways are a size heavier for the 4 m
more (the register).
The bay stands 0.50 m beyond the house's front, and the bridge deck is carried 1.10 m
beyond the bay all round as a gallery, from which its glass is washed and its wipers
reached.
The owner: "Of course needs doors to the deck outside the bridge". A weathertight door
in each wing's forward wall, beside the house's corner, opens outward onto the gallery,
hinged on its inboard edge; the gallery is 1.10 m wide so that the leaf (0.72 m) clears
the rail by 0.20 m through its whole swing.
NOT SETTLED
No scantling is calculated: the gallery's plate, face bar, knees and beams are
drawn at the sizes of the wings' own, and their welds to the front are not
designed.
The sight-line calculation JS4-402 is not run again with the bay; the line in
view C is this sheet's own.
The doors to the gallery stand in a forward-facing wall: their coamings are
0.15 m as her other bridge doors' are, and no rule was looked up for a door in
that position.
The general arrangement (JS1-102) still draws the wheelhouse as a rectangle to
5 m
